decision: Use DistilBERT by default because its predeclared primary metric and neutral-class F1 are materially higher. Accept the measured latency, size and maintenance costs for the local demonstration; retain TF-IDF as a lightweight fallback.
limitations: Amazon star ratings are distant labels rather than verified sentiment annotations.
The latency result describes one recorded local CPU and batch-one protocol.
The 90% selective-accuracy requirement was illustrative, not stakeholder validated.
Manual qualitative error coding was excluded from the final project scope; limitations are based on aggregate class, calibration, routing and slice evidence.

proposed_ui_policy.negative_positive_rule: apply the frozen DistilBERT confidence threshold
proposed_ui_policy.warning: The protected test diagnosed poor neutral selective accuracy. A future holdout or prospective evaluation is required before claiming that the revised policy meets a production accuracy target.

scope: local academic demonstration and analyst decision support
